questions.sec: The four stages & the first stage: latent vs active phase
questions.q: Match each stage of labour to its boundaries – 1st : 2nd : 3rd : 4th.
opts: True labour pain to full dilatation (10 cm) : full dilatation to delivery of baby : delivery of baby to delivery of placenta : 1–2 hrs observation after placenta
Onset of pain to engagement : engagement to crowning : crowning to birth : birth to placenta
True pain to 6 cm : 6 cm to full dilatation : full dilatation to birth : birth to placenta
Rupture of membranes to full dilatation : birth of baby : placenta : 24 hrs after placenta
questions.exp: 1st: true labour pain → full dilatation; 2nd: → delivery of baby; 3rd: → delivery of placenta; 4th: 1–2 hrs observation after placenta. (Book p499)

questions.sec: The four stages & the first stage: latent vs active phase
questions.q: Match the guideline to the latent-phase end / active-phase start dilatation – ACOG : New WHO : Old WHO.
questions.exp: ACOG: latent ends 5 cm, active begins 6 cm; New WHO: 4 cm / 5 cm; Old WHO: 3 cm / 4 cm. (Book p499)

questions.sec: The four stages & the first stage: latent vs active phase
questions.q: The characteristic EVENT of the latent phase is ______ while the active phase involves ______.
opts: Effacement + dilatation of cervix; dilatation of cervix + partial descent of fetal head
questions.exp: Latent phase = effacement + dilatation; active phase = dilatation + partial descent of fetal head. (Book p499)

questions.sec: The four stages & the first stage: latent vs active phase
questions.q: Duration of latent and active phases – Primigravida : Multigravida.
opts: Latent 12 hrs, active 4 hrs : latent 8 hrs, active 3 hrs
Latent 8 hrs, active 3 hrs : latent 12 hrs, active 4 hrs
Latent 20 hrs, active 6 hrs : latent 14 hrs, active 4 hrs
Latent 6 hrs, active 2 hrs : latent 4 hrs, active 1 hr
questions.exp: Primi: latent 12 h, active 4 h; multi: latent 8 h, active 3 h. (Book p499)

questions.sec: The four stages & the first stage: latent vs active phase
questions.q: Plotting of the active phase begins at ______ on the modified WHO partogram and at ______ on the WHO Labour Care Guide 2020; the latent phase is ______.
opts: 4 cm; 6 cm; plotted in the first column
questions.exp: Modified WHO partogram begins at 4 cm (old WHO); Labour Care Guide begins at 5 cm; latent phase is not plotted. (Book p499)

questions.sec: The four stages of labour
questions.q: Fill up: The first stage of labour ends with ______, and the fourth stage is defined as the first ______ after delivery of the placenta.
opts: delivery of the baby; two hours
delivery of the placenta; six hours
questions.exp: The stages are: first to full dilatation, second to delivery of the baby, third to delivery of the placenta, and fourth the first hour of observation. (Book p499)

questions.sec: Prolonged latent phase
questions.q: Prolonged latent phase is a latent phase lasting:
opts: ≥20 hrs in primigravida or ≥14 hrs in multigravida
≥14 hrs in primigravida or ≥20 hrs in multigravida
≥12 hrs in primigravida or ≥8 hrs in multigravida
questions.exp: ≥20 h in primigravida or ≥14 h in multigravida. (Book p499)

questions.sec: Prolonged latent phase
questions.q: Match the cause of prolonged latent phase with management – Unripe cervix : Occipito-posterior position : False labour pains.
opts: Prostaglandins (PGE1 & PGE2) : wait for spontaneous delivery : therapeutic rest (best)
questions.exp: Unripe cervix → PGE1/PGE2; OP position → await spontaneous delivery; false labour pains → therapeutic rest (best management). (Book p499)

questions.sec: Prolonged latent phase
questions.q: Prolonged latent stage as an indication for caesarean section – true or false?
opts: False – prolonged latent stage is NOT an indication for C-section
questions.exp: Note: prolonged latent stage is not an indication for C-section. (Book p499)

questions.sec: Prolonged latent phase
questions.q: Which of the following statements about a prolonged latent phase is TRUE?
opts: It usually reflects an unfavourable cervix rather than obstruction, so rest and analgesia are the treatment
It is an immediate indication for caesarean section in every case
It is always caused by cephalopelvic disproportion or a contracted pelvis
It should be treated at once with high-dose oxytocin augmentation
questions.exp: Therapeutic rest with analgesia lets an unripe cervix resolve; most women then enter the active phase or are not in true labour. (Book p499)

questions.sec: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
questions.q: Normal active-phase rate of cervical dilatation – Primigravida : Multigravida.
questions.exp: Dilatation: primi 1.2 cm/hr, multi 1.5 cm/hr. (Book p500)

questions.sec: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
questions.q: Normal active-phase rate of descent of fetal head – Primigravida : Multigravida.
questions.exp: Descent: primi 1 cm/hr, multi 2 cm/hr. (Book p500)

questions.sec: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
questions.q: Old vs new WHO recommendation on cervical dilatation:
opts: Old: minimum 1 cm/hr (basis of action line); New: <1 cm/hr can be normal and alert/action lines removed in Labour Care Guide
Old: 2 cm/hr; New: 1 cm/hr with alert line retained
Old: <1 cm/hr normal; New: 1 cm/hr minimum
questions.exp: Old WHO: minimum 1 cm/hr (basis of action line). New WHO: dilatation <1 cm/hr → normal; alert and action lines removed in Labour Care Guide. (Book p500)

questions.sec: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
questions.q: Protracted active phase is defined as cervical dilatation ______ OR descent of head ______.
opts: <1 cm/hr; <1 cm/hr in primigravida or <2 cm/hr in multigravida
Nil for 2 hrs; nil for 1 hr
questions.exp: Protracted active phase: dilatation <1 cm/hr (slow progress) OR descent <1 cm/hr (primi) / <2 cm/hr (multi). (Book p500)

questions.sec: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
questions.q: Management protocol for protracted active phase begins with vaginal examination — match the finding to the action: cephalopelvic disproportion : occipito-posterior position : inadequate contractions.
opts: CPD: caesarean section — occipito-posterior: wait for spontaneous rotation — inadequate contractions: assess them abdominally
CPD: wait and observe — occipito-posterior: caesarean section — inadequate contractions: start oxytocin
CPD: start oxytocin — occipito-posterior: caesarean section — inadequate contractions: wait and observe
CPD: amniotomy — occipito-posterior: forceps delivery — inadequate contractions: caesarean section
questions.exp: The finding on examination decides the action: disproportion is delivered, a good pelvis with malposition is given time, and weak contractions are assessed then augmented. (Book p500)

questions.sec: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
questions.q: If contractions are hypotonic/inadequate, augmentation of labour consists of:
opts: Artificial rupture of membranes and oxytocin
questions.exp: Augmentation = ARM + oxytocin. (Book p500)

questions.sec: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
questions.q: Sequence of augmentation – head engaged : head not engaged.
opts: ARM → 30 mins → oxytocin : oxytocin followed by ARM (↑ risk of cord prolapse)
questions.exp: Head engaged: ARM, then oxytocin after 30 min. Head not engaged: oxytocin first then ARM, because early ARM risks cord prolapse. (Book p500)

questions.sec: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
questions.q: Fill up: In the active phase of the first stage, cervical dilatation normally proceeds at least at ______ cm per hour.
questions.exp: A rate below about 1 cm per hour in a primigravida is protraction, which prompts a search for poor contractions, malposition or disproportion. (Book p500)

questions.sec: Arrest of active phase, arrest of descent & partogram of arrest
questions.q: Arrest of active phase is diagnosed when there is no dilatation of cervix for:
opts: ≥4 hrs despite good contractions (≥200 Montevideo units) OR ≥6 hrs of inadequate contractions despite oxytocin
≥6 hrs with good contractions OR ≥4 hrs with inadequate contractions
questions.exp: No dilatation ≥4 h despite good contractions (≥200 MVU) or ≥6 h of inadequate contractions despite oxytocin. (Book p500)

questions.sec: Arrest of active phase, arrest of descent & partogram of arrest
questions.q: Arrest of descent (a second criterion of arrest) = no descent of fetal head for:
opts: ≥2 hrs in primigravida, ≥1 hr in multigravida
≥1 hr in primigravida, ≥2 hrs in multigravida
≥4 hrs in primigravida, ≥2 hrs in multigravida
questions.exp: No descent for ≥2 h (primi) / ≥1 h (multi). (Book p501)

questions.sec: Arrest of active phase, arrest of descent & partogram of arrest
questions.q: Prerequisites for diagnosing arrest of active phase are ______ and ______; management is ______.
opts: Cervix ≥6 cm dilated; membranes ruptured; C-section
Cervix fully dilated; membranes ruptured; vacuum
questions.exp: Prerequisites: cervix ≥6 cm and membranes ruptured; management is C-section. (Book p501)

questions.sec: Arrest of active phase, arrest of descent & partogram of arrest
questions.q: On the illustrated arrest partogram, arrest of cervical dilatation appears as ______ and falling FHR indicates ______.
opts: A straight (flat) line for 3 hrs; fetal distress → immediate C-section
A line crossing the alert line only; wait
questions.exp: No dilatation for 3 h appears as a straight line; ↓FHR = fetal distress, an indication for immediate C-section. (Book p501)

questions.sec: Arrest of active phase, arrest of descent & partogram of arrest
questions.q: Other features on the same arrest partogram were meconium in amniotic fluid, 3+ moulding and good uterine contractions. In the FIRST stage, fetal distress is managed by:
questions.exp: In the 1st stage of labour, management of fetal distress is C-section only. (Book p501)

questions.sec: Arrest of active phase & arrest of descent
questions.q: A primigravida's partogram shows the cervix at 6 cm with no further change for four hours despite adequate contractions, and the head is at station zero. What is the diagnosis and next step?
opts: Arrest of the active phase — reassess for disproportion and deliver by caesarean section
Normal progress — continue to observe for another four hours
Prolonged latent phase — give sedatives and allow her to rest
Precipitate labour — prepare for immediate delivery
questions.exp: No cervical change for four hours with adequate contractions, or two hours without, is arrest of dilatation and needs delivery after excluding disproportion. (Book p501)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: The second stage of labour (from full dilatation of cervix, 10 cm) – main event, effect of epidural, and descent:
opts: Delivery of baby; epidural prolongs it by 1 hr; maximum fetal head descent occurs here
Delivery of placenta; epidural shortens it; no descent
Delivery of baby; epidural has no effect; descent minimal
Effacement; epidural prolongs by 2 hrs; descent begins
questions.exp: Main event = delivery of baby; epidural prolongs 2nd stage by 1 hour; maximum head descent occurs in this stage. (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: Fill the second-stage duration table for PRIMIGRAVIDA – average : maximum without epidural : maximum with epidural.
questions.exp: Primi: average 50 min, max 3 h without epidural, 4 h with epidural. (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: Fill the second-stage duration table for MULTIGRAVIDA – average : maximum without epidural : maximum with epidural.
questions.exp: Multi: average 30 min, max 2 h without epidural, 3 h with epidural. (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: Prolonged second stage without epidural is defined as:
opts: >3 hrs in primigravida; >2 hrs in multigravida
>2 hrs in primigravida; >1 hr in multigravida
>4 hrs in primigravida; >3 hrs in multigravida
questions.exp: Prolonged 2nd stage: >3 h primi, >2 h multi (without epidural). (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: Arrest of descent in the second stage requires a pre-requisite of ______ and management depends on ______.
opts: Normal FHR; maternal and fetal condition
questions.exp: Pre-requisite: normal FHR; management depends on maternal and fetal condition. (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: Fetal distress in 2nd stage with fully dilated cervix – management by station:
opts: Station above +2: C-section; station at +2 or below: forceps
Station above +2: vacuum; at +2 or below: C-section
questions.exp: Above +2 → C-section; at or below +2 → forceps (forceps preferred in fetal distress). (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: Which second-stage scenarios mandate C-section with NO instrumental delivery?
opts: Bandl's ring + prolonged 2nd stage; CPD + prolonged 2nd stage with moulding/caput
Prolonged 2nd stage with normal FHR at station +2
questions.exp: Bandl's ring or CPD (with moulding/caput) in a prolonged 2nd stage → C-section; instrumental delivery is contraindicated. (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: Prolonged 2nd stage with normal FHR and no CPD/obstructed labour – management:
opts: Station above +2: C-section; at +2 or below: forceps or vacuum
questions.exp: Above +2 → C-section; at/below +2 → forceps or vacuum. (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
questions.q: Requisites for instrumental delivery and the instrument of choice in fetal distress:
opts: Full cervical dilatation and station ≥ +2; forceps > vacuum
Cervix ≥8 cm and engaged head; vacuum > forceps
questions.exp: Requisites: full dilatation + station ≥ +2; in fetal distress forceps > vacuum. (Book p502)

questions.sec: Second stage of labour: durations
questions.q: Fill up: In a primigravida the second stage normally lasts up to ______ hours without epidural analgesia, and up to ______ hours with an epidural.
questions.exp: Two hours (three with an epidural) is the accepted limit in a primigravida, and one hour (two with an epidural) in a multiparous woman. (Book p502)

questions.sec: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring
questions.q: Obstructed labour is defined as:
opts: The baby cannot be delivered despite good contractions and full dilatation, from obstruction in the passage
Failure of the cervix to dilate despite adequate oxytocin augmentation
A latent phase lasting more than 20 hours in a primigravida
Delayed delivery caused by contractions that are too weak
questions.exp: Obstruction means mechanical blockage with adequate powers; weak contractions are inertia, not obstruction. (Book p503)

questions.sec: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring
questions.q: Obstructed labour is seen in all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Listed causes: transverse lie, conjoint twins, hydrocephalus, fibroid uterus. (Book p503)

questions.sec: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring
questions.q: On general examination in obstructed labour the mother appears:
opts: Exhausted, dehydrated, tachypnoeic with acidotic breathing
questions.exp: Exhausted, dehydrated, tachypnoeic, acidotic breathing. (Book p503)

questions.sec: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring
questions.q: Bandl's ring on P/A examination is the ______ between the ______ upper segment and the ______ lower segment.
questions.exp: Bandl's ring = groove between the tonically contracted (retracted) upper segment and the passively dilated (distended) lower segment. (Book p503)

questions.sec: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring
questions.q: Complications of obstructed labour include rupture of uterus and vesicovaginal fistula (VVF). The VVF appears:
opts: After 7-10 days, from ischaemic necrosis of the bladder with constant dribbling of urine
Immediately after delivery, from a direct laceration of the bladder wall
After six weeks, from a low-grade infection of the bladder
Within 24 hours, from trauma caused by the urethral catheter
questions.exp: Pressure necrosis declares itself a week or so later as continuous painless dribbling of urine per vaginam. (Book p503)

questions.sec: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring
questions.q: Management of obstructed labour and what must be AVOIDED:
opts: Immediate C-section + maternal resuscitation; avoid waiting, oxytocin and instrumental delivery
Wait for spontaneous delivery; avoid oxytocin
questions.exp: Immediate C-section with resuscitation; avoid waiting (↑ rupture risk), oxytocin and instrumental delivery. (Book p503)

questions.sec: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring
questions.q: All of the following are features of obstructed labour EXCEPT:
opts: A well-flexed deeply engaged head with no caput or moulding
A retraction ring rising obliquely across the abdomen
A tonically contracted tender uterus in an exhausted, dehydrated woman
A distended bladder, ketosis and a hot dry vagina
questions.exp: Obstruction produces marked caput and moulding with non-engagement; a well-flexed engaged head with no caput is a favourable, unobstructed picture. (Book p503)

questions.sec: Bandl's ring vs Schroeder's ring
questions.q: Match the alternate names – Bandl's ring : Schroeder's ring.
questions.exp: Bandl's = retraction ring; Schroeder's = constriction ring. (Book p504)

questions.sec: Bandl's ring vs Schroeder's ring
questions.q: Match the cause – Bandl's ring : Schroeder's ring.
opts: Obstructed labour : spasm of a uterine segment due to inadvertent oxytocin use
questions.exp: Bandl's ring results from obstructed labour; Schroeder's ring from spasm due to inadvertent oxytocin use. (Book p504)

questions.sec: Bandl's ring vs Schroeder's ring
questions.q: Match the site and stage – Bandl's ring : Schroeder's ring.
opts: Between upper and lower uterine segments, second stage : any site, first or second stage
Any site, first stage : between segments, second stage
Cervix, second stage : fundus, third stage
Lower segment, first stage : upper segment, second stage
questions.exp: Bandl's: junction of upper and lower segments in 2nd stage; Schroeder's: any site, 1st or 2nd stage. (Book p504)

questions.sec: Bandl's ring vs Schroeder's ring
questions.q: Palpability, visibility and maternal/fetal condition – Bandl's ring : Schroeder's ring.
opts: Palpable and visible P/A, maternal and fetal distress : palpable P/V, not visible, condition normal
Palpable P/V, visible, distress : palpable P/A, visible, normal
Not palpable, not visible, normal : palpable P/A, visible, distress
Both palpable P/A and visible with distress
questions.exp: Bandl's ring is palpable and visible per abdomen with maternal/fetal distress; Schroeder's ring is felt P/V, not visible and condition is normal. (Book p504)

questions.sec: Bandl's ring vs Schroeder's ring
questions.q: Relief of Schroeder's ring is by ______, and if C-section is needed the incision is ______.
opts: Stopping oxytocin and uterine relaxants (terbutaline), C-section if no relaxation; vertical (Kronig's) / lower vertical incision
Oxytocin increase; lower segment transverse incision
questions.exp: Schroeder's: cease oxytocin, terbutaline; C-section if no relaxation via vertical Kronig's / lower vertical incision. Bandl's ring is relieved by C-section. (Book p504)

questions.sec: Bandl's ring vs Schroeder's ring
questions.q: Match the ring with its description — 1) Physiological retraction ring 2) Bandl's ring 3) Constriction ring … A) A pathological ring that rises obliquely across the abdomen as obstructed labour advances B) The normal junction of active upper and passive lower segment that cannot be felt abdominally C) A localised spasm of uterine muscle around a fetal part, unrelated to the segmental junction
questions.exp: The physiological ring is normal and impalpable, Bandl's ring is the rising sign of obstruction, and a constriction ring is a focal spasm. (Book p504)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
questions.q: WHO recommended actions at admission in labour include all EXCEPT:
opts: Auscultate fetal heart sounds / P/V exam (contraindicated in active bleeding)
questions.exp: Not recommended: routine enema, routine pelvic examination, routine CTG, routine pelvic shaving. (Book p504)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
questions.q: Which of the following are NOT recommended routinely at admission per WHO?
opts: Routine CTG and routine pelvic shaving
questions.exp: Routine enema, pelvic examination, CTG and pelvic shaving are not recommended. (Book p504)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
questions.q: Ambulation in first stage – early labour : late labour/membranes ruptured.
opts: Allowed : lie in left lateral position
questions.exp: Ambulation allowed in early labour; left lateral position in late labour or after membrane rupture. (Book p504)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
questions.q: Oral intake in first stage and pre-C-section fasting rules:
opts: Solids not allowed, liquids allowed; for C-section stop solids 6 hrs and liquids 2 hrs before surgery
Solids and liquids allowed; stop both 8 hrs before surgery
Nil by mouth throughout labour; 12 hrs fasting before surgery
Solids allowed, liquids restricted; stop liquids 6 hrs before
questions.exp: Solids not allowed, liquids allowed; solids stopped 6 h and liquids 2 h before C-section. (Book p504)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
questions.q: Bladder function during first stage – the woman is encouraged to void every:
questions.exp: Encouraged to relieve bladder every 2 hours. (Book p504)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations for admission & first stage care
questions.q: Which of the following is consistent with WHO recommendations for care in normal labour?
opts: A companion of the woman's choice, oral fluids, freedom of movement and no routine enema or shaving
A routine admission enema, pubic shaving and nil by mouth for every woman
Continuous electronic fetal monitoring for every woman in labour
Routine episiotomy and routine early amniotomy to shorten labour
questions.exp: WHO supports respectful, low-intervention care; enemas, shaving, routine amniotomy and routine episiotomy are not recommended. (Book p504)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
questions.q: Which first-stage items (pain relief, companion of choice, ambulation, oral intake) are grouped under 'supportive care' in the Labour Care Guide?
opts: Ambulation, oral intake, pain relief and a companion of the woman's choice
Pain relief alone, since the others are obstetric interventions
Bladder care and fetal monitoring, which together define supportive care
An enema and perineal shaving, as recommended routinely on admission
questions.exp: Supportive care bundles the low-technology measures: mobility, fluids, analgesia and continuous support. (Book p505)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
questions.q: Monitoring frequency in the first stage – maternal pulse/BP : temperature (membranes intact / ruptured) : contractions : P/V.
opts: Hourly : hourly / 4th hourly : every 30 min : 4th hourly
Every 30 min : hourly / hourly : hourly : 2nd hourly
4th hourly : hourly / hourly : every 15 min : hourly
Hourly : 4th hourly / hourly : every 30 min : 2nd hourly
questions.exp: Pulse/BP hourly; temperature hourly (intact) or 4th hourly (ruptured); contractions every 30 min; P/V 4th hourly. (Book p505)

questions.sec: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
questions.q: FHR auscultation frequency – 1st stage low risk : 1st stage high risk : 2nd stage low risk : 2nd stage high risk.
questions.exp: 1st stage: 30 min (low risk) / 15 min (high risk); 2nd stage: 15 min / 5 min. (Book p505)

questions.sec: Management of second stage & prevention of perineal tear
questions.q: Recommended measures to prevent perineal tear include all EXCEPT:
opts: Controlled delivery of fetal head / modified Ritgen manoeuvre
questions.exp: Routine episiotomy and fundal pressure are NOT recommended. (Book p505)

questions.sec: Management of second stage & prevention of perineal tear
questions.q: In the modified Ritgen manoeuvre, one hand ______ and the other hand ______.
opts: Initially flexes then extends the fetal head; supports the perineum
Applies fundal pressure; pulls the head
Extends the head; presses the anus
questions.exp: One hand initially flexes then extends the head; the other supports the perineum. (Book p505)

questions.sec: Management of second stage & prevention of perineal tear
questions.q: Which statement about maternal position in the second stage is correct per the notes?
opts: Delivery can be done in any position
questions.exp: Note: delivery can be done in any position. (Book p505)

questions.sec: Management of second stage & prevention of perineal tear
questions.q: Fill up: Perineal trauma is reduced by applying ______ to the perineum in the second stage and by ______.
opts: warm compresses with hands-on support; avoiding routine episiotomy
a routine mediolateral episiotomy; fundal pressure
sustained Valsalva pushing; the lithotomy position
a routine episiotomy; early cord clamping
questions.exp: Warm compresses, hands-on support and spontaneous pushing reduce tears; episiotomy and fundal pressure increase trauma. (Book p505)

units.title: The four stages & the first stage: latent vs active phase
units.guide: Fix the boundaries of the four stages, then compare the latent and active phases by guideline cut-off, event and duration in primi and multi. Focus for this checkpoint: The four stages & the first stage: latent vs active phase.

units.title: Prolonged latent phase
units.guide: Define prolonged latent phase numerically and match each of its three causes with the correct management, remembering it is never a C-section indication. Focus for this checkpoint: Prolonged latent phase.

units.title: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase
units.guide: Learn the cm/hr benchmarks for dilatation and descent, the old vs new WHO 1 cm/hr rule, and the P/V-based protocol for slow active-phase progress. Focus for this checkpoint: Active phase: normal rates & protracted active phase.

units.title: Arrest of active phase, arrest of descent & partogram of arrest
units.guide: State the arrest criteria in hours and Montevideo units, the prerequisites for arrest of descent, and read the classic arrest partogram. Focus for this checkpoint: Arrest of active phase, arrest of descent & partogram of arrest.

units.title: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management
units.guide: Hold the average and maximum second-stage durations with and without epidural, then decide between C-section, forceps and vacuum by station and cause. Focus for this checkpoint: Second stage of labour: durations & arrest of descent management.

units.title: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring
units.guide: Recognise obstructed labour clinically, from the exhausted mother to the Bandl's ring, and know what to do – and what to avoid. Focus for this checkpoint: Obstructed labour & Bandl's ring.

units.title: Bandl's ring vs Schroeder's ring
units.guide: Contrast the retraction ring of obstructed labour with the oxytocin-induced constriction ring across cause, site, stage, palpability and relief. Focus for this checkpoint: Bandl's ring vs Schroeder's ring.

units.title: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care
units.guide: Sort the recommended from the not-recommended at admission, then apply the rules for ambulation, oral intake, bladder care, pain relief and monitoring frequency. Focus for this checkpoint: WHO recommendations: admission & first stage care.

units.title: Management of second stage & prevention of perineal tear
units.guide: List the four perineal protection measures, the two things not recommended, and the two-hand technique of the modified Ritgen manoeuvre. Focus for this checkpoint: Management of second stage & prevention of perineal tear.
